Crypto showed a modest bounce off a weekly low but remained in a broader downtrend tied to war-driven risk-off sentiment. yields.note: Treasury Secretary Bessent announced doubling long-end debt buybacks (10Y-20Y and 20Y-30Y sectors, $2B to at least $4B per operation, effective Sept 9). 30-year yield plunged from ~5.26% to as low as 5.18% (-9 to -10bp); 10-year fell from ~4.68% to ~4.63% (-5 to -6bp).

gold.note: Surged over 4% intraday, reaching the $4,480-4,500 zone — testing its daily 200-period SMA and breaking above a major descending trendline. Best single-day gold move of the week.

bitcoin.note: No clean same-day BTC figure retrieved — data gap. Broader crypto market remained in extended bear-market conditions per contemporaneous commentary.

dollar.note: Bloomberg reported the buyback announcement 'sending Treasury yields and the dollar down' — directionally weaker, magnitude not confirmed.

oil_geopolitical.note: US-Iran stalemate remained unresolved and kept inflationary risk in focus per FOMC-minutes commentary released the same day.

equities.note: S&P 500 closed +0.2%, Nasdaq +0.16% — stocks traded higher initially on the buyback news but faded through the day.

entries.causal_read: Clean textbook day: falling yields (opportunity-cost channel) + weaker dollar combined to drive gold's sharp rally. This is the clearest single-driver day of the three — good teaching example of the mechanism working as expected.
entries.confidence_overall: high for yields/gold relationship; BTC data gap remains

yields.note: Reversed sharply higher, giving back most of Wednesday's decline. 10-year climbed >5bp to 4.704%; 30-year rose ~6bp to 5.254% (one source noted a further +3bp on top of that later in the session). FOMC July minutes (released Wed) showed some officials favoring a rate hike this year to contain inflation — a hawkish overhang.

gold.note: Two-phase day. Early (pre-market/AM ET): gold extended Wednesday's rally, spiking to ~$4,510-4,520, still riding the falling-yield tailwind. Midday: eased back below $4,500 (~$4,474-4,491) as yields reversed. Evening (confirmed via Prof's live ThinkOrSwim position, ET close): gold reclaimed strength, position mark hit $4,573.60, +0.62% on the day — meaning gold finished UP on a day when yields were UP, breaking the simple inverse-correlation story.
gold.confidence: high — directly confirmed via live position screenshots at two points in the day

equities.note: Dow -350pts (-0.6%), S&P 500 -0.3%, Nasdaq -0.4 to -0.7% (5th straight losing day for Nasdaq). Walmart -8% on weak comp sales and soft guidance, dragged consumer staples sector -1.6% — a company-specific driver layered on top of the macro story.

entries.causal_read: This is the important teaching day. The simple 'yields up → gold down' story only explains the midday dip, not the evening reclaim. Yields stayed elevated all day, yet gold finished green. The more complete explanation: escalating Iran/oil geopolitical risk (a live, intensifying story on this specific day) likely dominated the yield effect by the close — safe-haven demand for gold outweighing the opportunity-cost drag from higher yields. Single-variable stories break down on exactly the days markets are moving the most — multiple drivers were fighting each other simultaneously, and geopolitical risk won.
entries.confidence_overall: high on yields/gold/oil/equities; BTC and DXY remain open data gaps for this date
